g.text: Canonical word recurrence: composed iteration
T-1525 | 2026-11-03 | producer checked; independent review pending
The new induction connects every UInt64 state to the previously checked ring recurrence.
Canonicality is derived at each iteration. The resulting observation sequence equals direct
polynomial evaluation in ZMod.
Canonical coefficients
Word iteration
(u,du,v) -> (add(u,du),add(du,dd),add(v,f))
Decoded ring state
Quadratic U, first difference D, linear V at every n
Ordered observations and final state
Old-state observations 0..p-1; final update at p retained
Validation records
Attempt 1: two Lean invocations, 17.042756 seconds; Difference passed, WordIteration rejected one
zero-cast type mismatch. Exact failed source and diagnostics are preserved.
Attempt 2: separately approved and frozen; five Lean invocations, 14.252913 seconds. Nine theorem
declarations and eight controls passed 17 named axiom readbacks. The false final-update equality was
rejected; three malformed axiom inventories were rejected.
Controls include constant padding, characteristic two, zero and late states, full wrap, retained
final update, the p=2^63 boundary, and overflow outside that bound. All 28,797 dependency/toolchain
file hashes match across the retained inventories.
Exact scope and next review
This proves the composed Lean word model, including ordered common-branch folds and canonical
zero/equality correspondence. Source mapping binds the native capture-before-update order. Rust
arrays, range iteration, compiler behavior and the remaining collector are separate refinement
obligations.
No primality premise is needed for the recurrence. Canonical natural representatives are not a
separately named theorem here. Existing full-sieve assumptions remain separate. No scientific
trajectories or performance ratios were produced.
A different author will review the published exact theorem/source correspondence and replay within a
prospective bound. JSON, CSV, source text, raw failure/success receipts and the archived logs
preserve the evidence for that review.
